The section describes the rigid per-mesh-bone pattern (CopyAbsoluteBoneTransformsTo: scene-node indexed, no inverse bind pose), which is not skinning; the heading now says 'A bone hierarchy without skinning (rigid parts)' and points to AnimationPlayer::GetSkinTransforms for skinned models.

dispositions.match: Dangling FNA3D_Device in FNA3D resource renderers
dispositions.reason: The card presented CNA's known_bugs.md entry on a dangling FNA3D_Device as an open task. At the snapshot the FNA3D resource renderers hold a shared device state cleared by the renderer, pinned by the Fna3d_Device_Lifetime test, and the second known_bugs.md entry (repeated SpriteBatch Begin/End on VULKAN) is pinned by Vulkan_SpriteBatch_MultiBeginEnd; the card keeps its slot and its Open badge and now says the two entries are stale (the Known Issues list carries the matching entry about the stale known_bugs.md text).

Language-binding support policy of 2026-09-26: C, C#, Java and TypeScript are the maintained bindings; Rust, Python, Ruby, Swift and Go are archived (not maintained, no forward compatibility guarantee, source and Git history being preserved in CNA Lab, libcna/cna-lab under bindings/). The cna-go row moved to the archived-bindings table; its final commit 510a84d is already reachable in cna-lab's history, so the row links https://github.com/libcna/cna-lab/tree/510a84da2ca799d4a15c8319f8ccf9e43df7a32a instead of the standalone repository that is due to be removed.
